fact: PactDigital, a government digital project, is set to extend mobile and internet connectivity to 1,000 underserved communities in 2026 under the 'Zero White Zones' initiative, benefiting 1.5 to 2 million people, mostly rural, per TechAfrica News citing the project.

Authorities are currently deploying telecommunications infrastructure in underserved areas and establishing digital community centres, according to the article on the National Forum on the Digitalization of Justice.
Data presented at the National Forum on the Digitalization of Justice showed internet access of about 72% in urban areas and 27% in rural areas.

On 30 September 2025 the Ministry launched the 'Zero White Zones' project to extend coverage to 750 rural zones without it, at FCFA 75 billion, with the State committing FCFA 37.5 billion via the FASU and PACTDIGITAL.
The article states 750 shared sites are planned in addition to 330 zones already connected since 2019, a closing line by the journalist.

The digital-transition minister said on 8 October 2026 that 750 villages would get calls, internet and mobile money for the first time by end-2026 and 750 more by 2028, with FCFA 25 billion mobilised by the State, under a zero-white-zone target for 2030.

At a 5 December 2025 workshop in Koudougou the ministry presented its project to cover 750 white zones in rural areas, 104 sites in the Nando region, within a goal of covering the whole territory by 2030, per the director general of electronic communications.
The communications minister launched the project to cover 750 white zones on 30 September 2025, with about 37.5 billion FCFA mobilised by the government and operators bearing the rest.
The minister said the State had subsidised the commissioning of 223 sites since 2020.
The minister said the government is committed to covering white zones by end 2027, with a 2025 target of connecting 750 more zones to basic electronic communication services.
The minister said 138 white zones were covered in 2024, built with a State subsidy via the Fonds d'accès au service universel (FASU).
The ministry's 2025 results list the launch of 750 further white-zone localities, and reducing white zones is among its announced 2026 infrastructure priorities.
The ministry reported covering more than 400 new white-zone localities in 2025.

The government launched pilot cases numériques with satellite internet in Doufiguisso and Lemnogo villages on 19 February 2026, with the FASU and UEMOA, and the current white-zone phase covers 750 zones with no mobile connectivity.
The article states that of 1,700 white zones identified, 283 were covered in 2022 and 138 in 2024.

The Ministry of Digital Transition, with funding from the FASU universal service fund and PACTDIGITAL, is running the national 'Zero zone blanche' project to cover 750 rural zones without network, including 66 localities in the Tannounyan region, with 4G sites planned over 8 to 12 months.
The ministry's rollout, after a first phase that already produced 138 sites, plans 750 sites in 2025 and 750 more in 2026.
Telecel Faso began deploying 300 telecom sites as part of the government's project to provide coverage to 750 underserved areas, reported by Connecting Africa.
Burkina Faso's government connected 183 'white zone' areas without network coverage in 2022 at a cost of CFA6.2 billion, per DCD citing Ecofin Agency.

Burkina Faso's government plans 800 telecom towers this year, 250 through the Digital Transformation Acceleration Project and 550 financed by the Universal Access and Service Fund (FASU), to reach 1,000 white zones by 2027, per DCD citing Ecofin Agency.

Agence Ecofin, citing official sources, reports that of 1,700 white zones identified in Burkina Faso 183 were covered in 2022 and 138 in 2024, with 750 planned for 2025 and the 2026 work plan of the digital ministry continuing coverage of the 750 white zones.
